transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I'm here because... well, for months now, I've been seeing the same pattern in my project files at work. I'm a translator, and certain subcontractors—and one colleague in particular—keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the file timestamps. 

They're doing it to make it look like my quality control failed. I've had our IT department look into it, and even though they tell me the audit trail is clean, I know what I'm seeing. The record has clearly been arranged to put the blame on me.
Have you been feeling unusually energized, irritable, or deeply depressed for extended periods of time while these events at work have been occurring?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, I haven't felt depressed or unusually energized at all. My mood has been pretty steady, honestly. It's a stressful situation to deal with, sure, but I haven't had any long periods of feeling down or overly irritable. I'm just working my regular hours.
Aside from the patterns you see in your work files, have you ever heard, smelled, or felt things that others around you seem unable to perceive?

No, nothing like that. I haven't heard voices or smelled anything unusual, if that's what you're asking. Everything else is completely normal. It's really just the digital files and the timestamps at work. I'm just seeing what's right there on my screen, nothing more.
Has this situation with your work files affected your relationships with your friends or family members?

With my friends and family? No, not really. Things outside of work are fine. 

But at the office... well, I haven't lost my job or missed any major deadlines or anything like that. It's just that project meetings have become pretty tense. I keep pressing them for the record to be corrected, and because of that, a few colleagues now avoid looping me into routine discussions unless they absolutely have to.
When the IT department tells you the audit trail is clean, do you believe they are also involved in the conspiracy against you?

I don't know if IT is actively in on it, honestly. It's more that... well, for months I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern in the project files. Certain subcontractors and one specific colleague keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the file timestamps. It's all done so it looks like my quality control failed. 

So, even when IT looks at the system and says the audit trail is clean, I just... I know the record has already been arranged to put the blame on me. IT might just be looking at a trail that was carefully covered up before they even got there. I know what I'm seeing on my screen.
Are there any other situations or people in your life, outside of your workplace, that you feel are working against you or acting in a suspicious way?

No, no one else. Outside of that specific project issue, everything is fine. I still do my regular translation work, I manage my team’s workflow, pay the bills, keep up with my family routines... all of that is perfectly normal. The only place things really go off track is when the file history or those certain coworkers come up. But outside of that, no, I don't feel like anyone else is working against me or doing anything suspicious.
How long have you been noticing these specific patterns in your work files?
I'd say it's been going on for about 11 months now. It started shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project.

Are you absolutely certain that these changes to the digital files are being made by human hands, or do you ever suspect that the files themselves are changing in ways that would be physically impossible for a person to accomplish?

No, it's definitely human hands. I mean, I'm not saying the files are magically changing on their own or anything impossible like that. It's just people logging in, making edits to the translation memory, and altering the timestamps. It's a very deliberate, manual process that they are doing to make me look bad. There's nothing supernatural or impossible about it, it's just... it's just them manipulating the system.

Outside of the stress caused by these incidents at work, have you noticed any decline in your ability to handle your daily responsibilities, such as your personal hygiene, your ability to manage your finances, or your social obligations?

No, not at all. Like I mentioned a minute ago, outside of that specific project issue, everything is fine. I still do my regular translation work, I manage my team’s workflow without any problems. I pay the bills, I keep up with all my family routines... my personal hygiene is fine, my finances are fine. The only place things really go off track is when the file history or those certain coworkers come up. But my daily responsibilities haven't been affected at all.

When you are speaking with your colleagues about these project files, do they ever mention that they have difficulty understanding your point or that your manner of speaking seems unusual or hard to follow?

No, not at all. I mean, my whole career is built on clear communication. They understand exactly what I'm saying. They might... you know, they might deny what they're doing when I confront them about the edits, or they just play dumb, but they've never said my speech is unusual or hard to follow. I make my points very clearly.
